correctness.rationale: Sufficiency uses an \(R\)-successor \(z\) falsifying \(\varphi\) at \(x\) and the exact condition to contradict any later \(y\) forcing \(\Box\varphi\) via a \(y\)-successor \(u\le z\). Necessity uses the persistent valuation \(V(p)=\uparrow R(y)\) when the condition fails. The two-point witness was checked directly, and a standalone exhaustive checker agrees with the atomic semantic criterion on every admissible labeled frame through three points.

value.rationale: The result closes the semantic gap highlighted by the motivating paper by replacing a merely sufficient frame condition with a necessary-and-sufficient one. The condition has a transparent confluence form, explains the published four-point counterexample, and yields the sharp smallest separation at two worlds. This is a structural correspondence and natural finite cutoff, not a routine parameter increment.
